new_format.axis_name: Format — what the ANSWER must contain
new_format.means: escape hatch — none of the above fits; write what you saw in the flag
new_format.requires: Tie-break:** read only the four options. If they are temperatures, the label is `calculate_value` or `recall_value` — never `pick_ratio`, however much ratio work the solution needs. `recall_value` vs `calculate_value`: is the value stored, or computed from the stem's numbers? `count_qualifying_items` vs `calculate_value`: counting was previously folded into `calculate_value` as "a small integer produced by counting", which hid a distinct task — nothing is computed, every listed item is adjudicated and the integer is the tally. `Q-000105` (how many species obey Hückel's rule, options 4 / 6 / 2 / 5) is the clear case. `pick_correct_statement` vs `pick_correct_combination`: are the statements printed as a lettered block the options then select from? Block → `pick_correct_combination`. Each option a standalone claim → `pick_correct_statement`. `pick_cause_or_effect` vs `pick_direction`: `pick_direction` is a spatial or rotational sense (eastward, clockwise, into the page). A quantity moving up or down **as a consequence** of a stated change is `pick_cause_or_effect`. `identify_structure_or_compound` vs `predict_product`: is a reaction printed? Reaction printed → `predict_product`. Four structures ranked on a criterion → `identify_structure_or_compound`. `pick_both_parts` vs E1 `multi_part_respectively`: these sit on different axes and usually co-occur. E1 records that the stem asked for several things; E2 records that the answer must get them all right together.

example_list.requires: assigning items to classes by a criterion

process.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

definition_term.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

definition_term.requires: explaining why a thing behaves as it does

classification_hierarchy.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept
classification_hierarchy.means: a scheme filing named entities into classes, groups, kingdoms or types, including the criterion that decides which box something sits in

diagram.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

structure_chemical.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

practical_procedure.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

reaction.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

nomenclature_rule.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

reaction_mechanism.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

disease_cause.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

graph.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

scientist_history.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

current_affairs.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

life_cycle.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

structure_function.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

experimental_observation.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

organism_characteristic.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept

new_shape.axis_name: Content shape — what is being tested, plus the actual concept
new_shape.means: escape hatch — none of the above fits; record it and flag it

recall.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
recall.requires: a rule applied to a case

concept_discrimination.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one

application.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
application.means: a stated rule, criterion or convention applied to this case. The rule must be known first — application is not knowledge-free

explanatory_reasoning.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
explanatory_reasoning.means: the live decision is whether one thing accounts for another

calculation.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
calculation.means: arriving at a number or expression by computing

representation_translation.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
representation_translation.means: moving between two representations of the same thing: an equation to a graph, a chemical name to its structure, a circuit to its equivalent

condition_based_reasoning.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
condition_based_reasoning.means: a rule applied under a stated condition that changes the outcome — the specified temperature, medium, reagent, or "battery disconnected"
condition_based_reasoning.requires: applying a rule with no condition attached

dimensional_reasoning.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
dimensional_reasoning.means: the relationship is derived or settled BY dimensions
dimensional_reasoning.requires: using dimensions to check an answer reached another way

single_step.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
single_step.means: one step, however much knowledge it needs

multi_step_dependent.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
multi_step_dependent.means: step 2 needs step 1's result. Four independent match-checks are NOT four steps

several_independent_checks.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
several_independent_checks.means: each item verified separately, verdicts combined
several_independent_checks.requires: 4c. `strategy_available` (zero or more, optional)** `elimination`, `estimation`, `symmetry`, `dimensional_check`, `unit_sanity`. **`elimination` requires a demonstrated shortcut:** name the one pair or fact and the options it strikes out — "fibrous → skull bones appears only in option 2". A recall question CAN offer elimination; that is no longer a contradiction, because recall is now a demand and elimination a strategy. **`dimensional_reasoning` (4a) vs `dimensional_check` (4c):** the same tool in two roles. If the question can only be answered by comparing dimensions, it is the demand. If dimensions merely confirm an answer the student reached by substituting into a relation, it is the strategy. **`condition_based_reasoning` vs `application`:** both apply a rule. The condition label is for the case where a stated condition is what the question turns on — remove the phrase "battery disconnected" or "in acidic medium" and a different option becomes correct. Its matching trap is `condition_ignored`. **4d. `new_demand`** — the escape hatch this axis was missing. If none of the five demands describes what the question makes the student do, record `new_demand` with a description and a flag. E1, E2, E3 and E5 each had one; E4 did not, so an unfamiliar demand had nowhere to go but the nearest fit. **Retired

multi_step.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one

explanation_based.axis_name: Thinking — three separate questions, not one
explanation_based.requires: The last three were retired in `scripts/build_category_sheet_v2.py` and never written down here, so for a while the rulebook could not account for 59 tags that the corpus carried. See Rule 21.

wrong_exponent.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

wrong_pairing.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

partial_combination.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

semantic_reversal.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
semantic_reversal.means: the relationship is reversed in words

unit_or_conversion.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
unit_or_conversion.means: a missing or wrong conversion yields it

intermediate_value.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
intermediate_value.means: a correct intermediate result is printed as an option

look_alike_term.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
look_alike_term.means: a term resembling the right one

true_statement_trap.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
true_statement_trap.means: the option is true but fails the task's polarity (NOT/EXCEPT)

other_one_fact.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
other_one_fact.means: a fact about a different member of the same family — another hormone, another organelle, another syndrome

neighbouring_fact.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
neighbouring_fact.means: a fact about an adjacent concept, disorder or event, where the families differ rather than the members

ignores_exception.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
ignores_exception.means: the option is correct for the general rule, and this question is the exception to it

scientist_swap.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

copied_from_stem.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

old_ncert_fact.requires: the change-log entry (Stage A), not an opinion

single_word_substitution.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
single_word_substitution.means: a long, fluent, almost entirely correct statement with one noun, adjective or negation swapped, so the surrounding truth vouches for the error

sign_reversed_magnitude_right.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
sign_reversed_magnitude_right.means: the magnitude and the method are right and one sign, right-hand rule or inequality is inverted
sign_reversed_magnitude_right.requires: the sign, and that the magnitude matches

wrong_power_of_dependence.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
wrong_power_of_dependence.means: linear where it should be squared, squared where it should be rooted, or a root dropped

neighbouring_question_answer.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
neighbouring_question_answer.means: the option is a real, published, remembered result that answers a DIFFERENT question the stem superficially resembles

sequence_endpoint_or_adjacency.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
sequence_endpoint_or_adjacency.means: an ordering that gets the ends right and fails on one interior adjacency, or reproduces the printed list order
sequence_endpoint_or_adjacency.requires: which adjacency, or that it is the printed order

parallel_order_decoy.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
parallel_order_decoy.means: the straight positional mapping A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV is offered as an option

true_but_out_of_scope.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
true_but_out_of_scope.means: the option is correct subject matter that answers a different question than the stem asked; it fails on relevance, not on truth

overclaiming_quantifier.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
overclaiming_quantifier.means: the option is wrong ONLY because of an "only", "all", "always" or "invariably"

fabricated_term.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

format_reflex_option.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
format_reflex_option.means: the option is the reflex pick for the printed FORMAT rather than for the content — "both true but R is not the explanation", or "both true and R explains A"
format_reflex_option.requires: the format, and why the content does not support the reflex

no_elimination_route.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
no_elimination_route.means: all four options are real terms from the same paragraph, so no securely-known fact strikes any of them out
no_elimination_route.requires: that all four are source terms of the same kind

complementary_grid.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
complementary_grid.means: the options are laid out as two magnitudes crossed with two signs, or two values crossed with two units, so no single error is self-evident

condition_ignored.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

condition_ignored.requires: the condition, and that the option is right without it

wrong_quantity.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
wrong_quantity.means: the option answers for a neighbouring PHYSICAL quantity: diameter for radius, moment of inertia for radius of gyration

wrong_site_or_stage.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
wrong_site_or_stage.means: the option moves a biological event to the wrong place or the wrong time
wrong_site_or_stage.requires: the real site or stage, and the offered one

omitted_contribution.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
omitted_contribution.means: one force, field contribution, circuit element or term is left out of an otherwise correct sum
omitted_contribution.requires: the omitted term and the option it yields

false_explanatory_link.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

false_explanatory_link.requires: the two true statements, and why the link fails

no_derivation_route.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
no_derivation_route.means: no arithmetic or factual route reaches this option at all; it widens the spread or completes a grid
no_derivation_route.requires: that no route exists — demonstrated, not asserted. **This is a property of the arithmetic, never a claim about what students would pick

new_trap.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
new_trap.means: a device none of the above describes
new_trap.requires: a full description; this is the axis's unsure form

source_damage_artifact.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

arguable_key.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

obviously_wrong.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
obviously_wrong.requires: "no student would be drawn to it" is a claim about students that inspection cannot support. But "no arithmetic or factual route reaches this option" IS inspectable, and a large share of the old tags were in fact our own extraction damage. The device was real; only its justification was not.

extreme_word.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
extreme_word.requires: the original was retired for treating "only" in a combination answer as an absolute-word trap. Reinstated with the counter-example required as evidence, so the quantifier alone is not enough.

sign_or_direction.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
sign_or_direction.requires: it was used for four unrelated things. The replacement must name WHAT reversed, so old tags are re-judged rather than renamed — but the tight case (all the work right, one sign wrong) is a real device and is now its own label.

number_near_miss.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
number_near_miss.requires: used where no numeric device was shown — in one case on a question with no numerical options at all. The only retirement with no inspectable form behind it.

wrong_order.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

unit_conversion_slip.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

task_polarity.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
task_polarity.means: direct, not, except, increasing, decreasing, maximum, minimum, respectively
task_polarity.requires: Materially changes what must be answered. Record NOT **in the task** only — not "does not" inside a biological premise, and not the NOT in standard A/R option wording.

review_status.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

concept.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing

key_checked_against.axis_name: Trap — one option, one mistake, or nothing
key_checked_against.requires: a tag is only as good as the question under it

elimination.means: name the one pair or fact and the options it
